discovery.none: No account-free or LAN discovery protocol is documented. Obtain the device MAC, enr and last-known IP from authorized Wyze cloud inventory, then confirm the current address against the router's DHCP lease for that MAC. A cloud IP can be stale; a different open port 88 is not proof.

identification.notes: Port 88 is not a discovery or identity signal. Identify only from the cloud model/type/firmware tuple and manually confirmed current LAN address. Do not scan for open ports and then assume a matching device.

device.name: Wyze Bulb Color / Light Strip (encrypted LAN)
device.notes:
SCOPE: only Wyze Bulb Color WLPA19C with cloud product_type MeshLight and Wyze Light Strip HL_LSL with cloud product_type LightStrip, on firmware for which the encrypted port-88 local API has been established. WLPA19C v2, WLPA19/WLPA19C BR30, HL_LSLP Light Strip Pro, white bulbs, plugs, cameras and every other model/type are excluded rather than inferred compatible.
Cloud inventory supplies the model, type, firmware, MAC, enr and last-known IP. All three model/type/firmware gates must be checked before a write; model alone is insufficient. The exact minimum compatible firmware is not established, so an unknown firmware version stops at identification rather than receiving a speculative command.
POST /device_request on TCP 88 can set attended light properties locally. HTTP 200 is only an acknowledgement, not proof of the resulting state. There is no documented local state-read schema in this spec: cloud property polling is still required for actual state. Do not invent a GET response, state_mapping, optimistic local state cache or local read entity.
identify_only is deliberate: this project has no consumer handler for the custom AES/padding/outer-JSON encoding. Ordinary power and light controls are documented as normal attended operations, not advanced operations, but a generic HTTP consumer must not send the plaintext endpoint body or render controls until such a handler exists.

openness.notes: This is an undocumented vendor-local interface reconstructed from public implementations, not a Wyze-published API or a claim about every mesh device or firmware release.

exclusivity.recovery: A light belongs to one Wyze account. Remove it in the old account or use its exact model reset before onboarding to a new account. HTTP client concurrency is not established; serialize writes per device.

pairing.notes: No separate LAN pairing window exists. Pulsing setup mode belongs to vendor onboarding, not authorization of a generic local HTTP client.

pin.notes: There is no local pairing PIN. Authorization is possession of the per-device enr obtained from the vendor cloud after account/developer authentication. BLE is used for onboarding, not a persistent client bond for this LAN endpoint.

unpair.clears: The vendor account binding when removed in the app; local enr revocation or rotation is not established.
unpair.notes: Removing a device from the cloud account is not proof that a copied enr stops working locally. For a compromised enr, reset and re-onboard, then refetch inventory; verify rotation before treating the old value as revoked.

issued_to_client: Wyze cloud session and developer API Key/ID for inventory and state polling
Per-device enr used as AES key and IV
Device MAC and last-known IP (addressing metadata, not credentials)
credentials.notes: The provisioning exchange's passphrase protection was not established. The local API uses reusable symmetric obfuscation, not per-client pairing or forward secrecy. Anyone holding enr and network access can construct a write; protect cloud inventory and local network access.

factory_reset.effect: Returns the selected light to vendor setup mode so it can be onboarded again. Refetch cloud inventory and enr afterward; whether enr rotates is not established. Do not use either procedure on a Pro, BR30, v2 or other excluded model.

procedures.basis: Wyze Bulb Color setup and factory-reset guides.
procedures.indicator: The bulb pulses slowly in setup mode.
procedures.name: Bulb Color: three off/on power cycles

steps.action: Using the wall switch controlling the WLPA19C Bulb Color, turn it off and on three times, completing the three cycles within six seconds with less than two seconds between toggles.
Wait for the bulb to pulse slowly, then set it up again in the Wyze app.
steps.expect: Slow pulsing confirms setup mode; no local command is sent during reset.

procedures.basis: Wyze Light Strip connectivity and factory-reset guide.
procedures.name: Light Strip: controller button held at least seven seconds

steps.action: With the HL_LSL powered, press and hold the button on the side of its controller for at least seven seconds.
Release when the strip starts pulsing and set it up again in the Wyze app.
steps.expect: Pulsing confirms setup mode; seven seconds is a minimum, not a maximum.

cloud.local_alternative: Local writes are possible only after this account/cloud-mediated setup and inventory. There is no account-free provisioning, enr-enumeration or discovery route. Cloud polling remains necessary for actual state.

methods.description: Complete vendor onboarding, authorize a client to the same Wyze cloud account, gate the exact model/type/firmware tuple, and only then send encrypted commands to the confirmed device address.
methods.name: Vendor BLE onboarding, cloud inventory, then direct LAN

stages.description: Use the vendor app with Bluetooth/location permission and a Wyze account. Bulb Color pulses after three power cycles; Light Strip pulses after its controller button is held at least seven seconds when a reset is needed.
stages.name: Vendor account and BLE onboarding to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi

steps.action: Sign in to the Wyze app and enable Bluetooth/location access. Select the exact Bulb Color or Light Strip product, not a Pro/BR30/v2 model.
Power the light and, if it is not already pulsing, use only its matching factory-reset procedure below.
steps.expect: Bulb Color or Light Strip pulses slowly in setup mode.

steps.action: Select the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network and complete onboarding in the vendor app.
steps.expect: The exact device appears in the owner's Wyze account.

cloud.local_alternative: The next stage provides local writes only after this inventory step. No account-free provisioning, enr retrieval or discovery exists; cloud polling remains required for actual state.

stages.description: Authenticate with the owner's Wyze account and developer API Key/ID. Match product_model and product_type exactly to one variant, then apply its firmware gate. Record MAC, enr, firmware and last-known IP; confirm the current IP by MAC at the router.
stages.name: Read and gate cloud device inventory

steps.action: Fetch the authorized cloud device list and select only WLPA19C/MeshLight or HL_LSL/LightStrip.
steps.expect: One exact model/type tuple is selected; every other tuple is rejected.

steps.action: Check the cloud firmware against the variant's firmware_gate and require a 16-byte ASCII enr plus MAC. Stop if firmware compatibility or enr is unknown.
steps.expect: The firmware and encryption prerequisites are explicitly established without probing an excluded model.

steps.action: Confirm the cloud last-known IP against the router lease for the same MAC; ask the user for the current address if it differs.
steps.expect: The target address belongs to the selected device, not merely to another service on port 88.

stages.description: Build protocol_details.local_mesh_api's inner and outer JSON exactly, POST to the confirmed address on port 88, and treat only HTTP 200 as transport acknowledgement. Continue polling cloud properties for state.
stages.name: Encrypted direct-LAN writes and cloud state polling

steps.action: Construct the inner mac/index/ts/plist object with a current Unix-epoch millisecond ts as a decimal string and only the declared property IDs.
Apply constant-0x05 padding, AES-CBC with ASCII enr as both key and IV, standard base64, and the documented outer slash escaping.
POST the compact outer JSON to http://<device-ip>:88/device_request and require HTTP 200.
steps.expect: Transport acknowledgement only; no power, brightness, Kelvin, color or mode state is inferred from the response.

steps.action: Poll the authorized Wyze cloud property/state endpoint for the resulting state and surface stale/offline state honestly.

setup.notes: Vendor account, BLE-assisted 2.4 GHz onboarding and cloud inventory are prerequisites. Direct LAN is the final stage of this ONE route, not an independent account-free setup method.

rejoin.notes: The reviewed vendor connectivity guides direct the owner through the model-specific reset and setup flow for a new network. No direct-LAN or account-free re-provisioning path is documented. After rejoin, repeat the cloud model/type/firmware gate and reconfirm MAC, enr and IP.

testing.notes: No bulb, strip, cloud account or local request was exercised by this project. The request encoding and property map are reported from public implementations. Invented test vectors prove encoding only, not hardware compatibility.

evidence.open_questions: Exact compatible firmware ranges, response-body semantics, enr rotation, offline longevity and the reliability of Light Strip writes remain open. No local state read is inferred from cloud property APIs.
evidence.public_implementation: wyzeapy's local request builder establishes the compact mac/index/ts/plist document, millisecond string timestamp, outer envelope and port-88 URL. Its encryption helper establishes direct ASCII enr key/IV and constant-0x05 padding. ha-wyzeapi establishes P1508=1 with RGB and P1508=2 with Kelvin. Nothing in those sources establishes a local state-read response schema.

http_endpoints.description: Documentary port-88 write endpoint. It requires the custom encoder in protocol_details.local_mesh_api and is not a generic plaintext JSON command. HTTP 200 acknowledges the request only; no local state-read schema is declared. Normal attended light operation, not an advanced firmware/configuration endpoint, but unavailable to this project's generic consumer while integration is identify_only.
http_endpoints.name: Encrypted mesh-light property write

fields.description: Standard base64 AES-CBC ciphertext; its outer JSON representation escapes every / as /.
fields.name: characteristics

covers: P1507 six-digit RRGGBB color and P1508 color/white mode
not_covered: Local state reads or acknowledgement-independent state confirmation
Effects, music mode, scheduling, groups and every property not listed here
All excluded models and unestablished firmware
local_access.summary: On an explicitly compatible model/type/firmware tuple, attended power, brightness, Kelvin, RGB and color/white-mode writes can be sent directly to the light after cloud onboarding and inventory.

MeshLocalAcknowledgement.description: Transport acknowledgement only, deliberately not a state envelope.
parse_rules: Require HTTP 200 before counting the write as acknowledged.
Do not infer a resulting property value from HTTP 200 or from an undocumented response body.
Use authorized Wyze cloud polling for actual state; no local state-read schema is declared.

encryption.base64: Standard RFC 4648 alphabet with +, / and = padding; never URL-safe base64.
encryption.iv: The same 16 enr ASCII bytes as the key.
encryption.key: The 16 enr ASCII bytes, used directly; do not hex-decode, hash, pad or UTF-16 encode the key.

padding.name: constant-0x05
padding.rule: Append byte 0x05 exactly 16 - (plaintext_length mod 16) times. This always adds 1-16 bytes, including a full sixteen-byte block when already aligned. It is NOT PKCS#7: do not append the pad LENGTH.

gate.address: Confirm the current IP by device MAC at the router; cloud IP alone may be stale.
gate.enr: Require exactly 16 ASCII bytes for this AES-128 profile.
gate.firmware: Require established encrypted-port-88 compatibility for the exact reported version; minimum versions are unknown and no range is inferred.

fields.mac: Uppercase 12 hexadecimal digits with no separators, from cloud inventory.
fields.plist: Array of {pid: string, pvalue: string} entries in the order shown by the selected property vector.
fields.ts: Current Unix-epoch time in MILLISECONDS as a base-10 JSON string, not seconds and not a JSON number.

mode_combinations.color: When explicitly selecting color, include P1507 RRGGBB followed by P1508=1 in the same plist.
mode_combinations.white: When explicitly selecting white temperature, include P1502 Kelvin followed by P1508=2 in the same plist.

P1507.pvalue_type: six ASCII hexadecimal digits RRGGBB without #; canonical vectors uppercase

inner_json.serialization: Compact JSON with no whitespace, preserving key order mac,index,ts,plist and pid,pvalue within each property.

outer_json.serialization: Compact JSON with key order request,isSendQueue,characteristics and no whitespace.

slash_escaping.rationale: JSON parsing turns / back into /, so the decoded characteristics value is standard base64. The public implementation performs an equivalent final JSON-string slash escape.
slash_escaping.safe_construction: Concatenate the fixed outer prefix, the base64 with / replaced by /, and the closing quote/brace. Do not URL-encode, switch to base64url, or emit \/ on the wire.
slash_escaping.wire_rule: Inside the characteristics JSON string, represent every base64 / as the two-character JSON escape /.

response.actual_state_source: Authorized Wyze cloud property/state polling remains required.
response.failure_handling: Timeout, connection refusal, non-200 or stale cloud state is not success. Do not silently turn a failed local write into a cloud write without the user's chosen fallback policy.

test_vectors.description: All MAC and enr values are invented documentation values. The expected ciphertext was independently generated with OpenSSL AES-128-CBC after the stated constant-0x05 padding.

remaining_unknowns: Minimum and maximum compatible firmware for each allowed model/type tuple are not established; unknown firmware must not receive writes.
The local response body beyond HTTP acknowledgement is undocumented and must not be treated as state.
Whether factory reset, re-onboarding or account removal rotates enr is not established.
Cloud IP freshness and operation during a prolonged cloud outage require hardware verification.
No local effects, music, schedules, groups, scene or state-read protocol is claimed.
